questions.question: What motivated you to go on exchange? (pick the most important one) *
questions.answer: Personal connection to the destination (heritage / friends there/ etc.)

questions.question: Which aspects were crucial to choosing your study destination? *
questions.answer: Knowing the language made it a lot easier to get around and communicate and also improve my skills.

questions.question: How would you rate your overall study abroad experience? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: Making lots of new friends and having the opportunity to travel and learn about the history while abroad.

questions.question: How easy was it to find the information you needed to know upon arrival? *
questions.answer: I found it a bit difficult as we barely got any information upon arrival. We didn't know until we were staying at the reception whether we had a dorm assigned to us or not. It would have been a help if we had the orientation day the very first day of the first week. I felt that I had to find out things on my own or with friends, and since I know the language, it was easier - not being able to speak the language would make it 100 times more difficult.

questions.question: What assistance, if any, did you receive when you arrived at your study destination? *
questions.answer:
I didn't really receive lot. I had to find out things on my own.
I knew where to show up for registration and to get the dorm.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the orientation and assistance available to students at your host institution upon arrival? *
Additional comments
questions.answer: It would have been a huge help if there could be tutors/older students on the first week/month.

questions.question: How did you find housing? *
questions.answer: I found housing through my host institution

questions.question: Did you live on campus or off campus? *
questions.answer: On campus

questions.question: What options were available for on campus housing? *
questions.answer:
Different types of dorms:
Single, shared (with 1-3 roommates but separate rooms and shared bathroom) or shared room and bathroom with one roommate.

questions.question: What options were available for meal plans or cooking facilities? *
questions.answer: Common area with washing machines and dryer and one electric stove on each floor.

questions.question: What should future exchange students know about living in on campus housing? *
questions.answer: Respect the rules. It's easy to hear noise from other rooms due to bad isolation. Bed sheets and bed linen are provided. Bed is a bit hard, but an extra mattress can be bought if necessary.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the housing available to students? *
Additional comments:
How easy did you find the registration process at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
Please describe the registration process at your host institution *
questions.answer: The website with courses is usually not updated, so you have to wait until they provide you the full list of courses sent by mail. The system to add and drop courses is in Chinese but guides are given beforehand. Don't stress, if you can't send the pre-approval of courses (forhåndsgodkendelse af fag). It's normal to have to wait a few weeks into the semester before sending it to your home university as the add and drop system will close later.

questions.question: What kind of help was available? *
questions.answer: Talking with friends.

questions.question: How successful were you in registering for the classes you wanted? *
questions.answer: For science majors, the courses are very limited. Fortunately, I was able to get enrolled in every course I applied for.

questions.question: What advice would you offer to future exchange students about registration at your host institution? *
questions.answer: More options of courses for business/economics students.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the academic programme at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
Were you a BA or MA student at UCPH when you were on exchange? *
questions.answer: MA

questions.question: Did you take BA or MA classes while you were on exchange *
questions.answer: BA

questions.question: Please elaborate on the level of courses *
questions.answer: All my courses were in English and the levels were adequate.

questions.question: How did the style of teaching at your host institution compare with that of UCPH? *
questions.answer: The grade depends on attendance, midterm, final exam and so on. All classes are in classrooms.

questions.question: How long were you on exchange? *
questions.answer: 1 semester

questions.question: Please list the courses you were enrolled in during your first semester. *
questions.answer: AI Ethics, Cellular and Molecular Imaging, Introduction to Science Writing and Communication in English, Learning and memory in the brain and Physiology.

questions.question: What specific courses would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: Introduction to Science Writing and Communication in English is a very helpful course to learn how to write a scientific paper/bachelor's or master's thesis.

questions.question: What items were more or less expensive than you expected? *
questions.answer: Everything is cheaper.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the non-academic opportunities (clubs, sports, etc.) at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
What kinds of cultural, athletic and social activities were available for students at your host institution? *
questions.answer: Running, many different student clubs (go to student fair in the beginning of the semester)

questions.question: Which non -academic activities would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: Language Partner Clubs - get friends with the local students. A good way to talk about cultural differences and overall get to know China better.

questions.question: What do you recommend other visiting students see or do on their weekends or holidays? *
questions.answer: Go to different cities in China by high-speed train but also staying in Beijing with friends - there are plenty of things to do. Enjoy the student life.

questions.question: How easy was it to adjust to the local culture of your exchange site? *
questions.answer: Have been to China before, so it was quite easy for me. I recommend reading up on Chinese culture and things you need to know upon arrival. For some, the culture chok may be big.

questions.question: Do you have any tips for socializing with local students?
questions.answer: Join the Language Partner Club and get to know the local students if there are none enrolled in the same class.

questions.question: What, if any, cultural differences did you find particularly challenging? *
questions.answer:
Some internationals students here are not used to squat toilets and that it's very normal to spit on the ground everywhere.
Language barrier.

questions.question: What parts of the culture did you most appreciate? *
questions.answer: People are friendly and willing to help.

questions.question: What are the three most important things you would tell a UCPH student who is going to your host institution on exchange? *
questions.answer:
Remember to also enjoy your time in Beijing and don't only focus on going travelling - you will only be an exchange student once/twice, but the city will almost always remain the same.
Remember to download all the necessary apps: WeChat, Alipay, Didi, Amap, Meituan, VPN.
Learn a bit Chinese beforehand, just the basics can help a lot.

questions.question: Is there any other information that you think might prove useful to future exchange students attending your host institution? *
questions.answer: Good idea to make a bank account here and buy phone subscription. They have bank and phone companies available. Buy a fridge for your dorm.

questions.question: What was the most rewarding part of your exchange experience? *
questions.answer: Making new friends from around the world and experience China with them.

questions.question: What was the greatest challenge during the exchange? *
questions.answer: Not easily being able to cook your own food. There's one electric stove, have to buy your own pots and pans.

questions.question: Any other comments?
Do you agree to share your travel report with other fellow students? *
questions.answer: Yes
